title: v1/chat.completions: preserve role metadata & introduce framed tool-output envelope for parity
author: Priya Raman
description: Context: Customers integrating Redwood through the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer reported two recurring issues: (1) role and custom metadata on assistant/tool messages getting lost during streaming/framing round trips, and (2) tooling/function outputs arriving as raw text blobs which made downstream structured parsing brittle, especially when stop token heuristics and logprobs are in play. Motivation: to improve parity with OpenAI semantics while keeping our streaming framing efficient and robust for function/tool calls. What this PR does: - Introduces a compact, backwards-compatible framed envelope for tool/function outputs (structured_output_v2) that carries: role, name, json_schema_hint (optional), and a base64-encoded payload when needed. This keeps streaming boundaries stable and keeps downstream parsers unambiguous. - Adds a preserve_role parameter mapping in the /v1/chat.completions adapter so role and any role-level metadata survive adapter translation and streaming framing. Default behavior remains backward-compatible. - Tightens stop token heuristics when framed envelopes are present: stop sequences are matched both at byte and token boundaries to reduce accidental truncation of structured payloads; we also avoid injecting artificial end tokens into the envelope body. - Ensures logprobs are attached to the correct top-level message tokens even when streaming emits intermediate frame boundaries; added a small KV-tagging scheme to re-associate token logprobs with message spans. - SDK surface: small TS and Python typing changes so that clients can opt into receiving structured tool envelopes instead of free-text tool outputs. - E2E regression tests and docs updates describing the new envelope and migration notes. Backwards compatibility and rollout strategy: the envelope is opt-in via a new adapter flag openai_compat.structured_output="v2" and a request-level param preserve_role=true. Default behavior preserves existing wire format (no frame envelope) so existing customers see no change. We will promote v2 by default in a minor release after a short canary. Related Linear: ENG-4132 (compat parity), PM-227 (docs/migration). Checklist: - [x] add envelope encoder/decoder (runtime) - [x] map preserve_role param in adapter - [x] update TypeScript/Python SDK types - [x] add e2e tests and flaky guardrails - [x] update docs/openai-compat.md - [x] add telemetry counters for envelope usage Commits: see commit_summaries.

review_comments: Ethan Powell (review): The framing approach looks solid — my main concern is perf overhead for small tool outputs. Can we prove zero-copy for small payloads?

Priya Raman (reply): We intentionally use a small header + optional base64 for binary-ish payloads. For pure text outputs we avoid base64 and serialize inline; added microbenchmarks in frame_encoder.rs showing <1% overhead for 512B messages.
Laura Chen (review): We need to ensure logs don't leak PII in telemetry.envelope_usage_counter. Please scrub any payloads and only emit metadata counts.
Priya Raman (reply): Agreed — the telemetry counter only records envelope type and size bucket, no payload. Added explicit redact tests.
Miguel Santos (approve): e2e looked good on canary; lgtm once CI green and docs have migration notes.

release_notes: Opt-in structured tool output envelope (structured_output=v2) and preserve_role mapping for OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity. Backwards compatible by default. See docs/openai-compat.md for migration steps and telemetry details.
